reasoning:
Let Z(n) = Σ_{i≥1} ⌊n/5^i⌋ be the number of trailing zeros of n!. Z is nondecreasing, Z(n) = Z(n−1) for n not divisible by 5, and Z(n) − Z(n−1) = v₅(n) when 5 | n. Hence a value k is skipped exactly when a jump has size ≥ 2, and each multiple of 5 with v₅(n) = j skips j−1 values. Equivalently, the number of skipped k in [1,K] is (number of multiples of 25 up to N) + (multiples of 125) + (multiples of 625) + ..., where N is the largest n with Z(n) ≤ K.

Locate N for K = 10000: Z(40000) = 8000+1600+320+64+12+2 = 9998; Z(40005) = 9999; Z(40010) = 10000; Z(40015) = 10001. So N = 40010 and every k ≤ 10000 that is attained is attained by some n ≤ 40010.

Skipped count = ⌊40010/25⌋ + ⌊40010/125⌋ + ⌊40010/625⌋ + ⌊40010/3125⌋ + ⌊40010/15625⌋ = 1600 + 320 + 64 + 12 + 2 = 1998.

Cross-check: distinct attained values in [1,10000] correspond one-to-one to multiples of 5 in [5, 40010], i.e. 40010/5 = 8002 values; 10000 − 8002 = 1998 skipped. Both methods agree.
